race.name: HYSK Gravel Classic Yakurai
race.tagline: Deep Tohoku gravel with 8,563 feet of climbing packed into 66 miles.

adventure.explanation: The long course loops through the mountain and agricultural landscape around Mount Yakurai, combining a high climbing load with rural Deep Tohoku scenery.

altitude.explanation: The challenge comes from repeated climbing rather than sustained high-altitude exposure.

climate.explanation: A late-August race in Miyagi adds summer heat, humidity, and changeable mountain weather without making climate the defining difficulty.

community.explanation: Kami Town, Hayasaka Cycle, and Panaracer jointly organize a three-day weekend with an expo, group ride, and welcome party, but the event is still building its international following.

elevation.explanation: The organizer lists 2,610 meters of climbing across 107 kilometers, an unusually dense 8,563-foot climbing day.

expenses.explanation: International travel to Japan plus the final transfer into rural Miyagi makes this an expensive destination race for most overseas riders.

experience.explanation: A hard race beneath Mount Yakurai, local food and culture, an expo, and nearby hot springs create a weekend that is more distinctive than a standard qualifier.

field_depth.explanation: UCI World Series status and qualification slots strengthen the field, though 2026 is the event's first World Series edition.

length.explanation: The official long course is 107 kilometers, or 66.5 miles.

logistics.explanation: The organizer gives clear venue and access guidance, but Kami Town still requires a car transfer of roughly 40 minutes from Furukawa Station or 70 minutes from Sendai Airport.

prestige.explanation: The race has national recognition and joins the UCI Gravel World Series in 2026, but it has not yet accumulated an international competitive legacy.

race_quality.explanation: A detailed schedule, seven checkpoints on the long route, a 700-rider cap, industry partners, and UCI sanction point to professional production.

technicality.explanation: Seventy percent of the long course is gravel and five categorized climbs per lap include pitches above 16 percent, but the organizer does not describe extreme singletrack or mandatory hike-a-bike terrain.

value.explanation: The 29,000-yen long-course entry is substantial, but it buys a full UCI race weekend rather than a bare local start line.

cultural_impact.explanation: The event is an emerging attempt to establish Kami Town as a Japanese gravel destination.

course_description.character: A two-lap mountain gravel race around Kami Town with 70 percent gravel and climbing that accumulates almost continuously.

suffering_zones.label: Opening climb
suffering_zones.description: The first categorized climb begins 1.9 kilometers into each lap and reaches an official maximum gradient of 18.2 percent.

suffering_zones.label: Mid-lap six-kilometer climb
suffering_zones.description: A 6.2-kilometer ascent beginning near kilometer 12.3 adds 272 meters before the course is halfway through a lap.

suffering_zones.label: Second lap
suffering_zones.description: The long-course categories repeat the full climbing sequence on the way to 2,610 meters of total gain.

course_description.signature_challenge: Fit 2,610 meters of climbing into a 107-kilometer race while preserving traction and pacing on the gravel sectors.

logistics.overview: The gravel race starts at 06:30 Saturday from Togei no Sato Sports Park, with registration Friday afternoon or early Saturday morning.
logistics.accommodation: The organizer links lodging options in Kami Town, Furukawa, Sambongi, Naruko Onsen, and Ginzan Onsen.
logistics.getting_there: The venue is about 40 minutes by car from Furukawa Station and about 70 minutes from Sendai Airport.
logistics.parking: The main venue is Togei no Sato Sports Park in Kami Town.
logistics.spectator_info: The weekend includes an expo, awards, a welcome party, and a separate Sunday group ride.

climate.overview: Late-August mountain and agricultural terrain in Miyagi can combine summer warmth and humidity with variable weather.
climate.wind_conditions: Exposed agricultural sections can make wind relevant even though climbing dominates the profile.
climate.altitude_effects: No high-altitude acclimatization is expected; repeated vertical gain is the physiological constraint.

terrain.terrain_overview: The organizer lists 74.4 gravel kilometers on the 107-kilometer long course through the hilly landscape around Mount Yakurai.
terrain.key_features: Two laps, five categorized climbs per lap, gradients up to 18.2 percent, and 2,610 meters of total climbing.

history.overview: Gravel events have run around Yakurai since 2021, with Hayasaka Cycle organizing Gravel Classic Yakurai from 2023 and the race joining the UCI Gravel World Series in 2026.
history.notable_editions: 2026 is the first UCI Gravel World Series edition.
history.growth_trajectory: A local gravel weekend has expanded into a 700-rider UCI qualifier backed by Kami Town, Panaracer, and Hayasaka Cycle.

final_verdict.one_liner: A real mountain-gravel test whose climbing density matters more than its 66-mile headline.
final_verdict.best_for: Strong climbers seeking an internationally sanctioned gravel race in a distinctive Japanese destination.
final_verdict.not_ideal_for: Riders looking for flat, fast gravel or an inexpensive international weekend.
final_verdict.pro_tip: Train for repeated low-cadence climbing, not just one long summit effort, and plan the final transfer into Kami Town before booking flights.
